sections.normalized_html: Right triangles [MATH: M N O] and [MATH: P Q R] are similar, where [MATH: M] corresponds to [MATH: P.] If the measure of angle [MATH: N] is [MATH: 35^{\circ},] what is the measure of angle [MATH: P?]

sections.normalized_html:
We are told that

  • the triangles [MATH: MNO] and [MATH: PQR] are right triangles,

  • [MATH: \triangle MNO \sim \triangle PQR],

  • [MATH: M] corresponds to [MATH: P], which implies [MATH: m\angle M = m\angle P],

  • and [MATH: m\angle N = 35^\circ.]

First, let's find the value of [MATH: m\angle M.]

Since triangle [MATH: MNO] is a right triangle and [MATH: m\angle N = 35^\circ,] the right angle cannot be at [MATH: M] because it is not among the given choices. Therefore, the right angle must be [MATH: m\angle O = 90^\circ.]

Now that [MATH: m\angle O = 90^\circ] and [MATH: m\angle N = 35^\circ,] we find [MATH: m\angle M] by subtracting from the triangle angle sum: [MATH: m∠M|= 180^{∘} − (m∠O + m∠N); = 180^{∘} − (90^{∘} + 35^{∘}); = 180^{∘} − 125^{∘}; = 55^{∘}]

Therefore, the measure of angle [MATH: P] is [MATH: m\angle P = m\angle M = 55^\circ.]

sections.normalized_html:
First, let's sketch the two triangles described.

Notice that

  • the segments [MATH: \overline{UV}] and [MATH: \overline{LM}] both lie on the vertical line [MATH: x=6,] and

  • the segments [MATH: \overline{UW}] and [MATH: \overline{LN}] both lie on the horizontal line [MATH: y=2.]

So, the angles [MATH: \angle U] and [MATH: \angle L] in [MATH: \triangle UVW] and [MATH: \triangle LMN,] respectively, are both enclosed by these perpendicular lines; hence, they are right angles.

We find the measure of [MATH: \angle V] using the fact that the sum of interior angles in a triangle equals [MATH: 180^\circ{:}]

[MATH: m∠U + m∠V + m∠W|= 180^{∘}; 90^{∘} + m∠V + (t^{∘} − 15^{∘})|= 180^{∘}; 75^{∘} + t^{∘} + m∠V|= 180^{∘}; m∠V|= 180^{∘} − 75^{∘} − t^{∘}; = 105^{∘} − t^{∘}]

Next, the measures of the legs of the triangle [MATH: \triangle UVW] are [MATH: UV|= 7 − 2 = 5,; UW|= 10 − 6 = 4,] and the measures of the legs of the triangle [MATH: \triangle LMN] are [MATH: LM|= (2 + 5k) − 2 = 5k,; LN|= (6 + 4k) − 6 = 4k.]

Hence, we have a pair of congruent angles,

[MATH: m\angle U = m\angle L = 90^\circ,]

and the lengths of the sides enclosing the congruent angles are in proportion:

[MATH: \dfrac{UV}{LM} = \dfrac{5}{5k} = \dfrac{1}{k} = \dfrac{4}{4k} = \dfrac{UW}{LN}.]

Consequently, [MATH: \triangle UVW \sim \triangle LMN] by the [MATH: SAS] similarity criterion, with the vertex correspondence

[MATH: U \leftrightarrow L, \qquad V \leftrightarrow M, \qquad W \leftrightarrow N.]

Therefore, the measure of angle [MATH: M] is

[MATH: m\angle M = m\angle V = 105^\circ - t^\circ.]

Item 2 — Example: Determining Measures of Corresponding Angles in Similar Triangles
